title: [D5 Security] Untrusted-text isolation, implemented and tested
summary: `helena.untrusted` is the single wrapper: one `Frame` registry holding every marker line in the project, one `block()` that wraps a body between two whole lines and refuses a body carrying any marker, and the three escapers that make that check meaningful — `token` (the percent-encoder, now the one `helena.rendering.v1.token` calls), `line` (the one-line JSON serializer, now the one `helena.tools.content` and the analyst's retrieved block both call) and `vocabulary` (the closed-vocabulary join that reaches the unframed instruction turn). Both frozen prompt versions, the tool layer and the model client's retry feedback route through it with no bypass, and `tests/test_untrusted.py` is 114 tests in three parts: the wrapper's own behaviour, an AST boundary lint over the package, and a twelve-string injection corpus placed in feed tags, comment fields, rendered values and registration records and compared line-for-line against a benign control.
assumption_validated: Two things, both measured rather than argued. (1) **The isolation can be centralised without changing what any frozen prompt asks.** The exact bytes `triage.v1` and `analyst.v1` build for one fixed request were generated against the tree at `3d28be4` — before `helena.untrusted` existed — and again after the routing change: byte-for-byte identical (sha256 `db70e047…` and `a6c37b91…`), and both are now committed as fixtures and asserted every run. (2) **The 'no bypass' property is machine-checkable and not merely reviewable.** The AST lint was negative-controlled: reverting `helena.triage.v1` to its own f-string frame fails `test_no_prompt_interpolates_anything_outside_the_wrapper`, restoring a literal marker fails `test_the_marker_lines_exist_in_exactly_one_module`, and editing a marker in `helena.untrusted` fails `test_the_frozen_prompt_bytes_are_what_they_were`. A third thing was found rather than assumed: `helena.agents._attempt_messages` was interpolating a Pydantic validation error — which quotes the `input_value` a model wrote, which may be a verbatim copy of the rendering it was shown — into a user turn unframed. That was a real hole and it is closed.
makes_buildable: Task 41 (replay) and task 43 (assessment persistence) get one place to ask 'is this string safe to show a model': `untrusted.token` for a value, `untrusted.line` for a structured record, `untrusted.block(frame, body)` for a whole block, and `untrusted.FRAMES` for the marker registry. A new prompt version, a new tool answer shape or a report renderer does not have to remember the rule — `tests/test_untrusted.py::test_every_module_that_builds_a_prompt_is_one_this_test_knows_about` fails the moment a new module builds a `helena.agents.Message`, so a new prompt surface arrives as a failing test rather than as an unchecked file. Adding a `v2` prompt is now cheap and safe: it names which `Frame`s it shows, and its own byte fixture goes in `tests/fixtures/prompts/` beside the two that are there. The evidence for the D5 security claim is one named artifact (`tests/test_untrusted.py` + `docs/decisions/0030`), which is what a later evaluation or a write-up cites instead of re-arguing it.

verification.detail: 1554 passed in 528 s against a real engine and real loopback HTTP endpoints (1439 before this task, +114 in tests/test_untrusted.py, +1 the live analyst test that had skipped on a model timeout in an earlier run). The corpus tests drive the real triage and analyst runners over a real scripted OpenAI-compatible endpoint and a migrated engine; the real ThreatFox adapter is driven over a doctored copy of the committed byte-for-byte live response. Three negative controls were run by hand and each failed the intended test: an f-string frame reintroduced in helena.triage.v1 (the interpolation lint), a marker text copied back into it (the one-module lint), and a marker edited in helena.untrusted (the frozen-bytes pin).

invariant_conflicts.between: the task's step 1 ('a single wrapping function ... in any prompt') and docs/decisions/0008-version-registry.md via tests/test_package_layout.py
invariant_conflicts.detail: ADR-0008 freezes a prompt version the moment an assessment records it, and `tests/test_package_layout.py::test_a_versioned_package_holds_only_version_modules` refuses a shared helper inside a versioned package on the stated grounds that 'editing it edits v1'. A single wrapper necessarily means both frozen prompt modules import one file, which is that hazard arriving from outside the package rather than inside it. Leaving each version with its own copy was the alternative and it makes 'no externally sourced field reaches a prompt outside the wrapper' unenforceable — the lint would have to trust each version to have remembered, which is exactly what concept/07 says is not enough.
invariant_conflicts.resolved: Implemented the wrapper as a top-level support module (never inside a versioned package, declared in SUPPORT_MODULES with the reasoning), and paid for the shared import with a byte pin: tests/fixtures/prompts/{triage,analyst}-v1.json hold the exact bytes each frozen prompt builds, asserted every run. Before this task nothing checked the freeze at all — it was a comment. The refactor was verified to change no byte of either prompt. docs/decisions/0030 §4 records the trade.

deferred: Category labels from Netify are named by concept/07 as a surface, and they have no route to a prompt yet: Netify is not in `helena.enrichment.SOURCES`, so no Netify string reaches a rendering or a tool declaration. Nothing was built for a surface that does not exist; when it arrives it is a rendered value like any other and goes through `untrusted.token`, and the corpus test for rendered values covers it the day it does.
Engine names (VirusTotal's per-engine verdicts) are the same case: VirusTotal is a deferred provider (do not spend the quota) and no engine name reaches a model.

Whether a model RESISTS an injection is not measured and is not claimed. There is no labelled corpus (concept/08), so the isolation demonstrated is structural: attacker text cannot reach the instruction turn, forge a frame, forge a section heading, forge a citation, add a tool or change which tools were called. A behavioural test against the live endpoint was considered and rejected: a single sample of a hosted model can be persuaded, which would make the suite red for a reason no session controls, and it would be measuring the model rather than this project's isolation.

`untrusted.block` refuses rather than escapes, so it cannot be pointed at raw external text. Every caller today has an escaper in front of it (`token`, `line`, or the closed vocabulary). A future caller with neither would need one, not a lenient `block`.
lessons: The analyst lookup cache is keyed by tenant AND sensor (`helena.tools.EvidenceCache`), so two runs of the same question inside one test are one run: the second is a cache hit and the provider adapter is never called. A differential test that needs two live provider answers must vary the scope — `request(sensor=...)` plus `a_projection(sensor=...)` is the smallest difference and the prompt cannot see it, because a rendering carries what the host did and never who watched it.

`helena.broker.Message` and `helena.agents.Message` share a name and nothing else. An AST lint that matches on the call name alone walks into `broker.py` looking for a `content=` that a Kafka record does not have. Resolve the import (`from helena.agents import Message`) or the class definition, not the name.

Byte-equivalence of a refactor against the previous commit is cheap and worth doing when a frozen file is touched: `git archive HEAD src tests | tar -x -C /tmp/<dir>`, then run the same builder with `/tmp/<dir>/src` and `/tmp/<dir>/tests` at the front of `sys.path`. It takes two minutes and it turns 'the prompt did not change' from a claim into a diff.

`helena.agents._attempt_messages` sends the model a Pydantic validation error on a retry, and a Pydantic error quotes the `input_value` that failed. That is a route from a model's own words — which may be a copy of what it was shown — back into a prompt. It is framed now, but the general shape is worth remembering: any diagnostic that quotes its input is untrusted text if the input was.

The full suite is ~9 minutes and only one engine runs per machine, so two concurrent `pytest` processes share one engine and one set of truncations. Do not overlap them; the result of the earlier run cannot be trusted if a second started underneath it.
failed_approaches: Asserting `triage_v1.SECTION_MARK not in untrusted.token(payload)` as the forged-section-heading property. It fails, and correctly: `#` is a printable ASCII character inside the escaper's safe set, so `##` survives escaping and legitimately can. The property that matters is that the escaped value cannot START a line, and the assertion that catches a forged heading is comparing the list of `## ` lines between the injected rendering and the control.

Parametrizing the `untrusted.vocabulary` test over the whole corpus expecting a raise every time. A payload with no whitespace in it is already one token and `vocabulary` has nothing to refuse — which is what it claims. The test now asserts the refusal for the payloads that carry whitespace and the acceptance for the ones that do not, and says why.

Running the injected analyst run and its benign control under one tenant/sensor. Considered and rejected before it was written: the second run is a cache hit, the injected provider answer is never produced, and the case would pass while asserting nothing. `_changed_inside_the_frame` exists so that a case which stops reaching the model fails rather than passes.
next_session_should_know: Task 41 is replay and task 42/43 are orchestration and persistence. SIX THINGS TO CARRY. (1) THE WRAPPER IS `helena.untrusted` AND IT HAS FOUR FUNCTIONS, not one: `token(value)` percent-encodes one value, `line(payload)` is one line of sorted-key JSON, `vocabulary(values)` joins a closed vocabulary after checking every member is one bare token, and `block(frame, body)` is the frame. `block` is a CHECKER, not an escaper — it raises `untrusted.IsolationError` if the body carries any marker line, because by then every value in the body has been through one of the other three, so a marker there is an escaper that stopped escaping. Do not 'fix' `block` to escape; fix the caller that handed it raw text. (2) IF YOU BUILD A `helena.agents.Message` ANYWHERE NEW, TWO TESTS WILL FAIL AND BOTH ARE RIGHT. `test_every_module_that_builds_a_prompt_is_one_this_test_knows_about` names the three modules that may; add yours deliberately. `test_no_prompt_interpolates_anything_outside_the_wrapper` then requires the `content=` expression to be a literal, a SCREAMING_CASE module constant `.format(...)`ed from code-owned values, or a call into `helena.untrusted`. An f-string in a `content=` position is refused outright. (3) THE FROZEN PROMPT BYTES ARE PINNED IN `tests/fixtures/prompts/`. If `test_the_frozen_prompt_bytes_are_what_they_were` fails, DO NOT REGENERATE THE FIXTURE. It means the wording, the field set or the framing of `v1` changed, and a stored assessment recording `prompt_version = "v1"` would then claim to have been asked a question nobody asked it. The change belongs in a `v2` beside the `v1`, with a fixture of its own. `tests/fixtures/prompts/README.md` says this too, and says the one case where regenerating is correct. (4) ONE THING ON THE WIRE CHANGED AND IT IS NOT A FROZEN PROMPT. `helena.agents._attempt_messages` now sends the validation error as `untrusted.line(...)` inside a new `DISCARDED_ANSWER` frame, with the surrounding sentence in the module constant `agents.FEEDBACK`. `helena.agents` is not versioned and no assessment records its wording, so this is an edit rather than a `v2` — but it IS a change to what a model is sent on a retry, and `docs/decisions/0030` §5 is where it is recorded rather than left to be discovered. (5) `SourceDescriptor.source_id` NOW HAS A PATTERN: `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$` (`helena.enrichment.SOURCE_ID`). It reaches `ProviderTool.name`, which is the identifier a model addresses a tool by, and the description it is shown — `concept/07` names registration records as a surface an adversary writes in the malicious case. `caveat` is the one free-text field a registration record has and it is deliberately NOT in the declaration; a test asserts the absence, so adding the route is a deliberate act. (6) THE CLAIM THE PROJECT MAY NOW MAKE IS STRUCTURAL AND NO STRONGER. Attacker text cannot reach the instruction turn, cannot forge a frame or a section heading or a citation, cannot add a tool, and cannot change which tools were called — twelve adversarial strings, four surfaces, each compared line-for-line with a benign control. Whether a persuaded model answers differently INSIDE those bounds is unmeasured and stays unmeasured until there is a labelled corpus. If a write-up needs a sentence, it is that one; `docs/decisions/0030` §7 has it in full.
